kai: Noticed repeated regressions when we combine aggressive prefetch + immediate compaction on idle. Prefetch pulls KV pages then compaction evicts/moves stuff and causes extra IO.

maria: Oof. So sequence is prefetch -> compaction -> request waits on IO. Can we order differently or add a lightweight lock?

jun: My thought: introduce a short "no-evict" lease per-request lifecycle (e.g., 100ms) that prevents compaction touching pages already touched by an in-flight request. Cheap to check via a per-slab epoch.

kai: Lease idea is good but must be cheap. We can keep a 64-bit slab_epoch and request stamps slab_epoch_read; compactor checks epoch changed since chunk start and yields. No heavy locking.

maria: Also add a prefetch hint: request.prefetch_profile = "minimal|aggressive". Minimal avoids pulling large KV spans for sub-200ms requests.

jun: Telemetry: prefetch_bytes_by_profile, compaction_yields_due_to_epoch, io_wait_ms_after_prefetch, in_flight_lease_count. Use these to tune default lease_ms per workload.

kai: Rollout: behind flag, default lease_ms=100, canary 2% tenants, collect telemetry for 48h, then increase. Add kill-switch to revert to previous behavior.

infra-bot: created /infra/checks/prefetch-lease-1839999001 4cb 4 checks pending

maria: Edge: ensure compaction checkpointing works if we abort mid-chunk. Jun please add resume markers.

jun: Will add chunk markers + idempotent resume semantics in the RFC/PR.

kai: Thanks, will draft RFC with API sketches and perf microbench (short bursts vs steady).
